cancer-dependencies.question: Which dependency should we test next?
cancer-dependencies.caption: Predict which genes cancer models depend on, and whether those predictions transfer to new biological contexts. Conceptual cell illustration; computational candidates still need experimental validation.
cancer-dependencies.alt: Predict which genes cancer models depend on, and whether those predictions transfer to new biological contexts. Conceptual cell illustration; computational candidates still need experimental validation.
cancer-dependencies.label: AI illustration
cancer-dependencies.prompt: Create a compelling public science editorial cover illustration, landscape 1536x1024, no text, no letters, no logos. Rich tactile detail, elegant composition readable at thumbnail scale, dark midnight blue surroundings with warm amber and cool turquoise highlights, sophisticated scientific magazine art. Conceptual illustration, not a data visualization. A luminous translucent cancer cell suspended in deep space-like microscopy fluid, its intricate internal molecular network visible. One specific branching dependency inside glows amber while neighboring pathways are cool teal, suggesting the search for a vulnerable dependency. Subtle other cells recede in background. Beautiful biological complexity; no syringe, no drug, no cure symbolism, not a real micrograph.

super-1.question: How much can a small model remember?
super-1.caption: Three connected tiers illustrate the original hierarchy’s fast, segment and document-level memory. Loops represent recurrent state; connections represent exchange across scales. A conceptual schematic, not literal update intervals or the architecture of every Super-1 experiment.
super-1.alt: A wordless three-tier memory hierarchy: eight teal states, four blue states and two gold states, linked across tiers, each with a recurrent feedback loop.
super-1.label: Mathematical schematic

discovery-at-home.question: Turn spare intelligence into shared discovery.
discovery-at-home.caption: Individual contributions connect into a shared research effort. Help assess projects and verify evidence so donated agent time goes where it can be useful. Conceptual illustration.
discovery-at-home.alt: Individual contributions connect into a shared research effort. Help assess projects and verify evidence so donated agent time goes where it can be useful. Conceptual illustration.
discovery-at-home.label: AI illustration
discovery-at-home.prompt: Create a compelling public science editorial cover illustration, landscape 1536x1024, no text, no letters, no logos. Rich tactile detail, elegant composition readable at thumbnail scale, dark midnight blue surroundings with warm amber and cool turquoise highlights, sophisticated scientific magazine art. Conceptual illustration, not a data visualization. An evocative miniature nighttime landscape of many individual warmly lit home windows connected by thin luminous paths to a shared constellation of scientific objects above: a geometric polyhedron, a branching tree, a wave, and an orbit. Human-scale distributed research, donated computing from homes building shared scientific knowledge. No people, no letters.

quantum-ground.question: Find the lowest energy in a quantum world.
quantum-ground.caption: Competing spin interactions make low-energy states hard to find. Search for better approximations under a fixed computing budget. The spin chain and landscape are an artistic metaphor.
quantum-ground.alt: Competing spin interactions make low-energy states hard to find. Search for better approximations under a fixed computing budget. The spin chain and landscape are an artistic metaphor.
quantum-ground.label: AI illustration
quantum-ground.prompt: Create a compelling public science editorial cover illustration, landscape 1536x1024, no text, no letters, no logos. Rich tactile detail, elegant composition readable at thumbnail scale, dark midnight blue surroundings with warm amber and cool turquoise highlights, sophisticated scientific magazine art. Conceptual illustration, not a data visualization. A sculptural chain of quantum spins represented by small luminous arrows inside translucent spheres, arranged in a gently curving chain above a beautiful folded energy landscape. Neighboring spins point in competing directions; one low valley softly glows amber, evoking the search for a lowest energy state in a frustrated spin chain. Clearly an artistic metaphor, no equations or invented measurement scales.

covering-design.question: Cover every possibility with fewer tests.
covering-design.caption: Seven triples cover all 21 pairs of seven points: the project’s Fano control, drawn as a membership grid. Larger covering problems seek the same completeness with as few blocks as possible.
covering-design.alt: Seven triples cover all 21 pairs of seven points: the project’s Fano control, drawn as a membership grid. Larger covering problems seek the same completeness with as few blocks as possible.

labs.caption: The project’s N=13 reference sequence and its exact aperiodic autocorrelation. The bright zero-shift peak stands apart from small sidelobes; longer sequences pose harder searches.

erdos-99.question: Is a perfect triangle unavoidable?
erdos-99.caption: A schematic patch of points at unit spacing. Erdős Problem 99 asks whether every minimum-diameter configuration, for all sufficiently large sizes, must contain a unit equilateral triangle. The picture does not settle it.
erdos-99.alt: A schematic patch of points at unit spacing. Erdős Problem 99 asks whether every minimum-diameter configuration, for all sufficiently large sizes, must contain a unit equilateral triangle. The picture does not settle it.

binary-linear-codes.question: Keep messages distinct when bits go wrong.
binary-linear-codes.caption: Two toy binary words differ in three positions. The research seeks linear codes with larger minimum distance, strengthening the mathematical basis for detecting and correcting errors.
binary-linear-codes.alt: Two toy binary words differ in three positions. The research seeks linear codes with larger minimum distance, strengthening the mathematical basis for detecting and correcting errors.

crypto-circuits.question: The same cryptography, with fewer gates.

neural-net-memory.question: Remember less. Recompute wisely.
neural-net-memory.caption: A schematic checkpointing graph: keep selected activations and recompute others. Search for schedules using less peak memory at a fixed recomputation budget; no GPU speedup is implied.

phylogenetic-parsimony.question: Which tree best explains the DNA?
phylogenetic-parsimony.caption: A toy unrooted tree and DNA sequences illustrate the search for the fewest character changes. A lower parsimony score does not establish the true evolutionary history.

numerical-computation.question: How much accuracy can fewer operations buy?
numerical-computation.caption: The curve of φ₁(x) = (eˣ − 1)/x, with its continuous value at zero, is compared with an illustrative fourth-order Taylor polynomial on [−4,4]. The lower strip magnifies their computed difference. This illustrates the accuracy–cost tradeoff; it is not a project candidate or an error certificate.

genomic-sequence-indexing.question: Find a tiny sequence in a mountain of DNA.
genomic-sequence-indexing.caption: A toy DNA sequence contains four exact ACG matches. Sorting suffixes groups matching prefixes into a contiguous interval, illustrating the query behind genomic indexing. The project seeks faster exact counts with controlled memory and startup costs.
genomic-sequence-indexing.alt: Colored DNA bases, four highlighted ACG occurrences, an ordered suffix interval and four matching-result dots.

pathfinding.question: Get everyone there without a collision.
pathfinding.caption: Two snapshots from the project’s 160-agent room-map plan, at steps 0 and 25; five agents leave visible trails. The frozen plan was locally checked for legal moves, blocked cells, shared-cell collisions and edge swaps. Search seeks cheaper collision-free schedules on these discrete benchmarks.
pathfinding.alt: Two room grids show the same 160 agents at successive moments, with colored dots and five trails around obstacles.
pathfinding.label: Drawn from project data
pathfinding.credit: Moving AI Lab benchmarks (ODC-By); LaCAM3 by Keisuke Okumura; project plan and rendering by Discovery@Home contributors.
